description: This Australian CISC advisory guides owners and operators of critical infrastructure in the Communications Sector on assessing risks, to complement the Critical Infrastructure Annual Risk Review. It notes that natural hazards are becoming more prevalent with longer-lasting impacts, and that the sector is vulnerable because its assets are nationally dispersed and often remote. Risks are presented under the hazard categories of the Security of Critical Infrastructure Act 2018 and the critical infrastructure risk management program rules of 2023, covering identification of relevant impact on availability, integrity, reliability and confidentiality, risk considerations by hazard category, threat and hazard prioritisation, and sector interdependencies. Producer: Critical Infrastructure Security Centre, February 2026, nine pages. Coverage: Australia. Access: free PDF; the first pages were read and the hazard sections were not read in detail. Licence and cost: free; no licence statement read. Caveats: general guidance, not a dataset, and it states it is not legal advice. Simulation uses: the hazard categories, impact definitions and interdependency notes structure resilience and hazard-exposure scenarios for communications assets. Related record: the BEREC public warning and emergency access databases (data-berec-public-warning-and-emergency-access-databases).
